Create a single cohort criterion

Source: R/criterion.R
cf_criterion.Rd

A cf_criterion represents one inclusion or exclusion step in a cohort eligibility pipeline. Five step types are supported (see type). The predicate is always a one-sided formula or a function; the interpretation depends on the step type.

Usage

cf_criterion(
  predicate,
  label,
  type = c("include", "exclude", "group_include", "group_exclude", "select_within",
    "randomise"),
  by = NULL,
  category = NULL,
  arms = NULL,
  reason = NULL
)

Arguments

predicate

A one-sided formula or a function.

  • For include / exclude: evaluated row-wise; must return a logical vector of length nrow(data).

  • For group_include / group_exclude: evaluated in a dplyr::summarise() context per group (defined by by); must return a scalar logical. The result is broadcast back to all rows in each group.

  • For select_within: evaluated per group; must return a logical vector identifying which rows within the group to keep.

  • For randomise: must be NULL (a randomise step never removes rows).

Formula predicates are evaluated with a data mask, so the rlang pronouns work in every step type: .data$age always refers to the column and .env$age to a variable in the formula's environment, which avoids ambiguity when a column and a local variable share a name.

label

A short human-readable description of this criterion.

type

One of "include", "exclude", "group_include", "group_exclude", "select_within", or "randomise".

by

For grouped step types (group_include, group_exclude, select_within): one or more character strings naming the grouping column(s); supply more than one for composite (multi-column) grouping. For randomise: one or more character strings naming the randomisation unit column(s) (e.g. "cluster_id"). Must be NULL for the row-wise types (include, exclude). Rows with an NA in any by column cannot be assigned to a group and are always removed by grouped step types.

category

An optional character string grouping this criterion with others for display purposes (e.g. "Valid age" to group age-related steps into one box in a CONSORT diagram). NULL (default) leaves the step uncategorised (NA in output).

arms

For type = "randomise" only: a single character string naming the column in the data that holds each unit's allocated arm (e.g. "arm"). Used by as_consort_diagram()/as_attrition_tibble() to default branch_by when not explicitly supplied. Must be NULL for all other types.

reason

An optional short description of the rows this step removes, used wherever removals are listed: the exclusion boxes of as_consort_diagram(). NULL (default) falls back to label for the exclusion types (exclude, group_exclude), whose label already describes the removed rows. For include, group_include and select_within the label describes the rows kept, so set reason (e.g. label = "Aged 18 or over", reason = "Under 18"). Must be NULL for randomise. See the Labels section of include().

Value

A cf_criterion object (an S3 list).

See also

Other criteria builders: cf_criteria(), check_criteria(), exclude(), group_exclude(), group_include(), include(), randomise(), select_within()

Examples

# Row-wise inclusion
cf_criterion(~ age >= 18, label = "Adults only", type = "include")
#> [+][~] Adults only
#>     age >= 18

# Grouped under a category, with the text shown for the rows it removes
cf_criterion(~ !is.na(age), label = "Age recorded",
             type = "include", category = "Valid age", reason = "Age missing")
#> [+][~] Age recorded
#>     !is.na(age)
#>     removes: Age missing

# Group-level inclusion (clusters with >= 5 participants)
cf_criterion(
  ~ n() >= 5,
  label = "Sufficient cluster size",
  type  = "group_include",
  by    = "cluster_id"
)
#> [+][~] Sufficient cluster size [by: cluster_id]
#>     n() >= 5

# Select first operation per patient
cf_criterion(
  ~ consent_date == min(consent_date, na.rm = TRUE),
  label = "Index operation",
  type  = "select_within",
  by    = "participant_id"
)
#> [>][~] Index operation [by: participant_id]
#>     consent_date == min(consent_date, na.rm = TRUE)

# Randomisation marker (no predicate; excludes nothing)
cf_criterion(
  predicate = NULL,
  label = "Randomised",
  type  = "randomise",
  by    = "cluster_id",
  arms  = "arm"
)
#> [R][-] Randomised [by: cluster_id] [arms: arm]
#>     <none>
